risk_if_not_implemented: Without Prohibition On Unverified Hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), cloud-hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) may be misconfigured, over-exposed or governed inconsistently with on-premises controls. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Lack of oversight of third-party controls (R-GV-7), Harm from Unauthorized / Unintended Product or Service Use (R-SC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Software Usage Restrictions
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce software usage restrictions to comply with applicable contract agreements and copyright laws.
compensating_control_1.justification: Software Usage Restrictions (CFG-11) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Prohibition On Unverified Hosted Assets, Applications & Services (CLD-13) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Third-Party Management
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of third-party management controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Third-Party Management (TPM-02) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Prohibition On Unverified Hosted Assets, Applications & Services (CLD-13) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
